thread:
Anna Patel: quick sync — proposing a "phased gatekeeper" layer to deconflict canary/fallback signals across tenants/regions. Right now observers sometimes all trigger and we end up with duplicate rollbacks or noisy oscillation. Idea: gatekeeper ingests normalized signals, applies tenant-specific weight & safety policy, emits a canonical decision event (soft-degrade / full-fallback / no-op). Thoughts?
Mike Chen: makes sense. main worry is centralization = latency SPOF. Could we do region-local gatekeepers + a global reconciler? keep per-tenant fast path local, fallback to global for wide correlation.
Devon Reyes: agree on hierarchical. also we need a compact signal schema — don't bake metric names. propose a single signal envelope: {type, value, window_secs, provenance, confidence}. then policies operate on envelopes. e.g. error_rate, model_quality, p99_latency, drift_score.
Sarah O'Neal: +1. also need smoothing/ debounce rules and cooldowns. otherwise short blips cause churn. propose params: window=60s, smoothing=exponential(alpha=0.3), min_consecutive_windows=2, cooldown=10m, ttl=5m.
Lee Zhang: implementation nit: for local gatekeepers we can use lease-based leader election (k8s endpoints or consul) so decisions are deterministic per-region. Global reconciler reduces risk of conflicting actions. avoid CRDT complexity — we need clear owner for enforcement.
Anna Patel: tradeoffs: deterministic owner -> simpler enforcement & audit, but more coupling. probabilistic hedging (randomized traffic shift) reduces rollbacks but complicates SLAs. suggest default soft-degrade: step traffic down to X% for N minutes before full rollback. keep config-driven.
Mike Chen: agree. we also need an observability contract for decisions: every canonical decision must include contributing signals, weights, and counterfactuals for explainability. otherwise SRE/PM can't debug. add trace_id and example requests sample.
rollout-bot: deploy-bot: canary detection: tenant="acme" region="us-west-2" reason="p95_latency > 1200ms" action="propose_soft_degrade(50%)" :warning:
Devon Reyes: I'll draft an RFC with the following interface sketches: POST /report_signal -> ack, stores envelope; GET /decision?tenant=...&since=... -> current canonical decision; server-sent events stream /events for realtime decisions. Version signals with "schema_v". Example payload:
```json
{
  "schema_v": "1",
  "tenant": "acme",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "signal": {
    "type": "p95_latency_ms",
    "value": 1350,
    "window_secs": 60,
    "provenance": "observer-42",
    "confidence": 0.95
  }
}
```
Sarah O'Neal: include policy fragment example too — we need to express soft-degrade thresholds, min-traffic, and rollback_action. something like:
```yaml
policy:
  - metric: p95_latency_ms
    threshold: 1200
    action: soft_degrade
    degrade_steps: [80,50,20]
    window: 120
    consecutive: 2
    cooldown: 600
```
Anna Patel: nice. next steps: Devon can you put up the RFC with the API + policy DSL + proposed telemetry fields? also add tests for missing signals (simulate observer outages) and skewed clocks. ping me when ready.
Mike Chen: add chaos tests for partial partition (region gatekeeper unreachable) — ensure global reconciler doesn't flip everything to fallback.
Lee Zhang: question: who owns execution? gatekeeper should emit decisions; enforcement happens in the router component which must be idempotent and able to accept duplicate canonical events. include idempotency key + intended_effect in the event.
Devon Reyes: noted. will include event schema: {decision_id, tenant, intent: {type, params}, contributing_signals: [...], ttl, issued_by, sequence}. enforcement idempotency via decision_id.
Anna Patel: sweet. small ops ask: add a metric for decisions_per_min and avg_time_from_signal_to_decision. we need SLO on decision latency.
rollout-bot: FYI @channel the current prototype on staging already emits decision_id and contributing_signals. will wire to staging router tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Sarah O'Neal: :+1: good progress. thanks all — RFC to review next week.
